summary: A strong first Bangkok temple choice if you want a spectacular indoor highlight plus time wandering an extensive historic complex. The enormous gilded Reclining Buddha is the headline; courtyards, tiled chedis and quieter corners reward staying beyond the photo stop. This remains a working place of worship, so expect modest clothing, shoe removal and respectful behaviour.
whyGo: See the Reclining Buddha at close range and appreciate its scale within its hall.
Combine ornate temple architecture and Buddhist heritage with a walk around Tha Tien.
The temple's traditional medicine and massage association adds another layer of interest; treatments require separate planning.
bestFor: Photographers willing to work around other visitors
skipIf: You are already tired of temple visits
You need a fully air-conditioned outing
Your main goal is a guaranteed quiet attraction
duration: Allow 1–2 hours as a planning estimate; add time separately for massage and queues.
cost: Official website: foreign visitors 300 THB per person; Thai nationals free with valid national ID. Massage, transport and guides are additional; current treatment prices not verified.
hours: Official homepage lists 08:30–19:30. Its visitor-planning search listing says 08:00–19:30, so plan around 08:30 and reconfirm individual hall access before a late visit.
bestTime: Aim for the start of the visiting day to make outdoor walking more comfortable and improve the chance of fewer tour groups.
gettingThere: Official address: 2 Sanam Chai Road, beside the Grand Palace in Tha Tien. Sanam Chai MRT is a useful nearby approach; check your walking route and active entrance in a map before setting out.
booking: An independent visit can be planned around admission at the temple. No advance reservation requirement was identified on the official homepage; guide requests and massage should be checked separately.
accessibility: A complete step-free route, accessible toilet provision and access inside the Buddha hall were not verified. Contact the temple about your specific mobility needs; do not assume historic thresholds and shoe-removal areas are wheelchair accessible.
practicalTips: Wear clothing covering shoulders and knees and shoes that are easy to remove.
Bring water and sun protection for the outdoor sections.
Pair with Tha Tien food or another nearby sight, leaving a break between temple visits.
Check directly with the temple rather than relying on unsolicited claims that it is closed.
decemberNotes: Plan extra flexibility for holiday visitors and arrive early. No December 2026 special opening programme or closure calendar was verified; check official announcements near the date.
uncertainties: Official pages disagree about opening at 08:00 or 08:30.
Last entry, individual hall closing times, payment methods and December exceptions remain unverified.
Massage availability and detailed accessibility need direct confirmation.
